check.title: an unpaid request is answered with status 402
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md, Payment Required Signaling: "The server indicates payment is required using the HTTP 402"

check.title: the 402 carries a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header

check.title: PAYMENT-REQUIRED is base64 of a JSON object

check.ambiguity: the spec never names the base64 alphabet or padding; the tool accepts standard and URL-safe, padded or not

check.title: the base64 variant matches the spec examples (standard alphabet, padded)
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md examples use the standard alphabet with = padding

check.title: PaymentRequired.x402Version is the number 2
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: x402Version, number, Required, "must be 2"

check.title: PaymentRequired.resource is an object with a string url
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: resource, object, Required; ResourceInfo.url, string, Required

check.title: resource.url designates the requested resource
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: url, "URL of the protected resource"
check.ambiguity: the spec does not say whether url must equal the request URL byte for byte; the tool reports the relation

check.title: ResourceInfo optional fields respect their bounds (serviceName, tags, iconUrl, description, mimeType)
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: serviceName printable ASCII max 32; tags max 5, each printable ASCII max 32; iconUrl absolute http(s) max 2048

check.title: PaymentRequired.extensions, when present, is an object
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: extensions, object, Optional

check.title: every advertised extension is an object with info and schema objects
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: Extensions table, info object Required, schema object Required

check.title: an extension's info validates against its own schema
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: schema "JSON Schema defining the expected structure of info"; extensions/bazaar.md: "Facilitators must validate info against schema before cataloging"
check.ambiguity: the core text defines schema as describing info; a server whose info fails its own schema advertises something no facilitator would catalog. Sign-In with X is excluded: its example schema describes the client's proof, not the challenge

check.title: payment-identifier info.required, when present, is a boolean
check.clause: extensions/payment_identifier.md, `required` Field: Type boolean, Default false
check.ambiguity: the example schema lists required among its required members while the field table gives it a default; an absent value is read as false, not as a failure

check.title: how the payment-identifier schema expresses the 16..128 character bound on id
check.clause: extensions/payment_identifier.md, `id` Format: Length 16-128 characters; the example schema uses minLength 16 and maxLength 128

findings.detail: minLength 16, maxLength 128 as in the example

check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: accepts, array, Required

check.title: accepts offers at least one payment method
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: "Array of payment requirement objects defining acceptable payment methods"
check.ambiguity: the text does not forbid an empty array; a 402 without any offer cannot be paid, so the tool warns

check.title: every accepts[] entry has scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo (strings) and maxTimeoutSeconds (number)
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: PaymentRequirements table, all six Required; extra, object, Optional

check.title: every accepts[].network is a CAIP-2 identifier
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: network, "Blockchain network identifier in CAIP-2 format"; 11.1 "{namespace}:{reference}"

check.title: every accepts[].amount is a decimal integer string of atomic units
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.1.2: amount, string, "Required payment amount in atomic token units"
check.ambiguity: no grammar is given; a non-negative decimal integer is the only reading consistent with the examples

check.title: reserved extra keys carry their section 6.1 meaning: paymentFlow is authorization, upfront or escrow; assetTransferMethod is a string
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1: "clients and servers MUST interpret them as defined here"; flow table

findings.detail: asset and payTo are addresses (1 offer(s))

check.title: asset transfer methods offered on eip155 networks
check.clause: schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md: eip3009 (default), permit2, erc7710

check.title: the 402 body (free for the server to choose)
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md, Response Body: "Response bodies are a server implementation concern"

check.title: browser clients can read the x402 headers (Access-Control-Expose-Headers)
check.clause: not a spec clause; needed only by browser clients

check.clause: not a spec clause; a client that reads the terms then pays relies on it

check.title: a malformed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE is answered with status 400
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md, Error Handling: "Invalid Payment | 400 | Malformed payment payload or requirements"

check.title: error reasons given on refusals

findings.detail: not base64: invalid_payment; base64 of plain text: invalid_payment; base64 of an empty object: invalid_payment; accepted matching no offer (amount changed): invalid_payment; unknown scheme: invalid_payment

check.title: how a payload marked x402Version 1 is treated
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.2.2: x402Version Required; a v2 server may also keep accepting v1 payloads for compatibility, which the v2 text neither requires nor forbids
check.ambiguity: not judged: the core text makes x402Version an identifier and invalid_x402_version a code for an unsupported version, without forbidding an endpoint that serves several versions; what happened is reported

check.title: a payment that cannot be valid (zero signature) never yields the resource
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1: "at least one check ... MUST run before the resource executes. The resource never executes with nothing checked"
